playbook.intent: A distributed team burns its fifteen-minute sync on people reading their own git history aloud to each other. The change holds when the pre-brief — merges per person, blocked PRs, red CI jobs, fresh Sentry or Datadog regressions — is in the channel before anyone joins, and the call has measurably shrunk against its old length because only blockers get spoken.
playbook.scope: Distributed team walks into the 15-min sync with the AI pre-brief already posted in the channel: yesterday's merges per person, blocked PRs, failing CI jobs, Sentry/Datadog regressions, today's intended focus. Standup runs on exceptions, not status theater.

success-criteria.criterion: The pre-brief is in the channel before the meeting opens, assembled from git history, the issue tracker and chat rather than typed by a person
Measured sync length has fallen against the pre-change baseline and the meeting is capped at ten minutes
A weekly accuracy score for the pre-brief exists alongside the prompt diffs that came out of it
The team has recorded a keep, change or drop call on the AI pre-brief instead of letting it run on inertia

stage.name: Set the Pre-Brief
stage.intent: AI does the boring summary before humans meet.

tasks.task: Pick the AI tool and connect it to issues / chat / git history
Define the pre-brief template (yesterday, blockers, risks)
Time-box the human standup to 10 minutes max

stage.decision-gate: Advance only when pre-brief is delivered to channel before the meeting.

stage.name: Run It Daily
stage.intent: Use the pre-brief; don't re-read it aloud.

tasks.task: Team reads pre-brief 5 minutes before standup
Standup discusses only blockers and decisions, not status
Update pre-brief prompts when accuracy drifts

stage.decision-gate: Advance when standup time has dropped vs baseline.

stage.name: Tune & Retro

tasks.task: Once a week, score pre-brief accuracy and usefulness
Decide: keep / change / drop the AI pre-brief

stage.decision-gate: Required output: a written weekly tune note.
